declared.note: This file must be committed before any hardware run. Its value is its timestamp: pinned after the fact it proves nothing.

expected_at_threshold.note: (Q,Q) is deterministic at every gamma -- the outcome is always CC, so on a noiseless device all shot noise comes from the (dev,Q) arm.

expected_device_bias.direction: downward: the measured crossing should land AT OR BELOW gamma_c, never materially above it
expected_device_bias.mechanism: depolarizing noise pulls both payoff curves toward the uniform-mixture value 2.25. The (dev,Q) curve, which is falling through 3.0 at the threshold, is dragged down faster than the flat (Q,Q) curve, moving the crossing left.
expected_device_bias.simulation_note: isolated at 200k shots per point, so the shot-noise floor (~0.0011 rad) is well below the residual

pass_criterion.falsified_if: the measured crossing lies outside the tolerance, lies materially ABOVE gamma_c (the bias direction is predicted), or no sign change is found in the swept range at all
pass_criterion.rationale: shot noise alone is NOT the whole error budget: a real device biases the crossing downward by an amount comparable to the 3-sigma shot tolerance. Pre-registering shot noise only would have set a criterion the hardware fails for reasons unrelated to whether the EWL threshold is correct. Both terms are fixed here, in advance, and neither may be widened after the run.

deviation_strategy.why: at gamma=pi/2 the best reply to Q is Q, so an argmax taken there returns Q and the deviation gain is identically zero

protocol_fixed_in_advance.estimator: last sign change of (payoff(dev,Q) - payoff(Q,Q)), linearly interpolated between adjacent grid points
